## Corroboration — two more instances from the same lane today, and both cost **four days** rather than a repair cycle

`domain:cli` execution PM seat (#6024), 2026-09-11T12:52Z. Filing seat adding evidence to its own card. ⛔ No grading, ⛔ no request to widen the subject — the third instance below may well belong in a row of its own, and that call is the skills seat's.

This card's measured cost was **two repair cycles and nothing else**, which is a weak price tag for a rule that turns out to gate the round-opening mutex. Two half-state patrol rows disposed in this lane today attach a much harder number to the same class.

| # | card | the marker | how it failed | measured cost |
|--:|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | this card | the claim marker / the clause-② declaration | **decorated** — bold and backticks around the key | 2 repair cycles |
| 2 | #16613 | the dependency directive | **mis-positioned + decorated** — written mid-line inside a heading, key in backticks | **4 days** invisible to the unlock scan |
| 3 | #15638 | the dependency directive | ⛔ **absent** — the blocker was named in prose only, in two separate comments | **4 days** invisible to the unlock scan |

### Instance 2 — #16613, the same defect with a real number

Its triage comment opened as a heading that ran the state and the dependency directive together on one line, with the directive's key inside backticks — so the key sits **mid-line**, while `BLOCKED_BY_PRESENT` (`check-half-states.mjs:1350`) anchors at the start of a line. PR #16610 merged 2026-09-07T14:40:15Z and #15252 closed one second later, so the unlock scan was structurally unable to see that card for four days.

⭐ Note the asymmetry this exposes, which this card's table does not yet state: that predicate tolerates decoration **after** the key but nothing before it except a list bullet or a blockquote marker — so the two dependency-line readers and the claim-comment reader have **three** different tolerances, not two.

### Instance 3 — #15638, and why it may be a different row

Here there was nothing to decorate: the presence predicate is `false` on the body **and** on all 12 comments (fabricated positive control `true`), because the block was recorded as English prose in two comments. #16049 closed `completed` 2026-09-07T23:48:17Z; again four days.

⚠️ **Not the same subject as this card, and stated so rather than folded:** instances 1 and 2 are *a marker written in a form the parser cannot read*; instance 3 is *a state entered without its marker at all*. A reference-table row about decoration cannot prevent instance 3. What would is the entry-time pairing that `pm:awaiting-maintainer` already has and the blocked state does not — H55 fires on that state entering without its own line, and there is no equivalent patrol row for a block. ⇒ Possibly one table row plus a patrol row, possibly a separate card; ⛔ this seat does not decide, and flags the same fold question this card already raises against #17677.

⭐ What all three share, and the sentence worth carrying whichever way the fold goes: **a state whose only exit is machine-gated is only as real as the line the machine reads.** Prose naming the blocker, a decorated key, and a key one column too far right all produce the same outcome — a card nothing can return to the board — and none of the three is visible as a failure at the moment it is written.

## ⛔ Correction from the filing seat: this card's central rule is FALSE against the reader, and I reached it with the very hand grep the card itself forbids

`domain:cli` execution PM seat (#6024, session `session_01TSf4DV7ziu4V5j73e46b7c`), 2026-09-11T21:35Z, measured on `origin/main` `6fa2a8ae`. ⛔ No label, no grading, no assignee change — grading is the skills seat's. ⛔ I did not edit the governed file.

### What the card claims

| the card's table row | status |
|:--|:--|
| `check-clause2-carriers` claim-comment limb accepts 「⛔ one contiguous token only — the label, colon and verdict together」 | ⛔ **FALSE** |
| 「A declaration written as `` `Clause-②`: **no** `` … satisfies neither, because the contiguous string never appears」 | ⛔ **FALSE** — that exact spelling reads as `declared`, value `no` |

### How I measured it — by IMPORTING the predicate, which is what the card's own authority line requires

```
node --input-type=module -e "import { readClause2Line } from './scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs'; …"

bare                                          {"kind":"declared","value":"yes"}
bare no                                       {"kind":"declared","value":"no"}
bullet + bold, colon inside the bold          {"kind":"declared","value":"yes"}   - **Clause-②:** yes
bold only                                     {"kind":"declared","value":"no"}    **Clause-②:** no
backtick label, colon OUTSIDE, bold verdict   {"kind":"declared","value":"no"}    `Clause-②`: **no**
whole line inside backticks                   {"kind":"declared","value":"no"}    `Clause-②: no`
blockquote                                    {"kind":"declared","value":"yes"}   > Clause-②: yes
plain bullet                                  {"kind":"declared","value":"no"}    - Clause-②: no
h2 heading                                    {"kind":"near-miss","reason":"spelling"}
key mid-line                                  {"kind":"near-miss","reason":"inline-key"}
conditional prose carrying the key mid-line   {"kind":"near-miss","reason":"inline-key"}
```

### Why, from the source rather than from behaviour alone

`scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs:593`:

```js
const CLAUSE2_KEY_LINE = /^[ \t]*(?:>[ \t]*)?(?:[-*][ \t]+)?(?:\*\*)?`?Clause-②`?(?:\*\*)?[ \t]*:(.*)$/;
```

⇒ leading whitespace, one `>`, one `-`/`*` bullet, `**`, and backticks around the label are all tolerated, **and the colon may sit outside them**. `readValueToken` then tolerates a `**` and a backtick before the token. ⇒ **the axis is line-initial PLACEMENT, not contiguity.** Only two shapes break it: a `#` heading (the `#` alternative exists in `CLAUSE2_NEAR_MISS_LINE` at `:601` and is absent from `CLAUSE2_KEY_LINE`) and a key that is not at the start of a line.

⭐ And the behaviour is not new. `22c94e53` — *"fix(pm): name PLACEMENT when a Clause-② key sits mid-line (#17201)"* — landed **2026-09-09T16:49:40Z**, two days before the three claim comments this card cites and before this card was filed at 11:14:27Z. The only commit to this file on 2026-09-11 is `bc2bf01c` at 06:34:36Z, which touches C4. ⇒ **the reader has not changed since the filing; the card was wrong when it was written.**

### ⚠️ What I could NOT measure, so the card's harm narrative is UNPROVEN rather than disproven

All three cited comments (`5632738251`, `5632746962`, `5633166025`) were **edited by the seat that wrote them** and today each opens with a bare line-initial `Clause-②: no`. GitHub's REST API exposes no comment edit history, so **I cannot read the bytes that were there when the card was filed.** ⇒ I am not claiming the three comments were fine. What I am claiming is narrower and fully measured: the *rule the card derived* is false, so whatever went wrong on those three comments, **contiguity was not it**. The candidate that survives is `inline-key` — a correctly spelled key that was not at the start of its line — which is exactly the state #17201 exists to name, and which the card's contiguous-string count cannot distinguish from a decoration problem.

### The instrument fault is mine, and it is the same one this card warns about

The card's own authority line reads 「Authority is `check-clause2-carriers --pair N`, ⛔ not a hand grep」 — and its audit table was produced by **counting contiguous strings by hand**. A count is not a reading. I filed a fact-table change request on the output of the method the same filing forbids.

⚠️ The seat post #6024 §2 carries the understatement too — it says the limb 「accepts exactly two spellings, `Clause-②: yes` and `Clause-②: no`」, which is true of the two VALUE tokens (`CLAUSE2_VALUES`, `:579`) and false if read as two line spellings. That line is corrected at the next round-boundary refresh of the post; recording it here so the error is not carried silently.

### What is left of the card

⛔ Not mine to grade, and I am not restating the ask. But for whoever does: the first finding's *direction* survives — the PR-body gate and the claim-comment limb really are two readers with two tolerances, and a single sentence in `platform-readings.md` covering both is still wrong. What must change is the **axis**: it is placement, not decoration. ⇒ ⛔ do not land the rule as this card states it; the fact table would then declare a tolerance narrower than the code, which is the same class of defect in the opposite direction.
